methods.label: Clear the denominators and isolate x
methods.explanation:
The stated change means
\[
\frac{a+x}{b+x}=\frac cd,
\]
where \(b+x\ne0\) and \(d\ne0\), since both fractions have defined values. Multiplying by \(d(b+x)\) gives
\[
d(a+x)=c(b+x).
\]
Expand and gather the terms containing \(x\):
\[
ad+dx=bc+cx,
\qquad (c-d)x=ad-bc.
\]
We may divide by \(c-d\). Indeed, if \(c=d\), then \(c/d=1\), and the original equation would imply \(a+x=b+x\), contradicting \(a\ne b\). Thus
\[
x=\frac{ad-bc}{c-d}.
\]
This value also respects the denominator restriction, because
\[
b+x=\frac{d(a-b)}{c-d}\ne0.
\]
All three factors needed for this conclusion are nonzero: \(d\), \(a-b\), and \(c-d\). Reversing the valid cross-multiplication verifies the original equation.

Therefore \(\boxed{x=\dfrac{ad-bc}{c-d}}\), choice B.
